title: Automated rollback failures during multi-variant model rollout — rescue runbook & ops controls
creator: Ava Park
description: Summary: During a staggered multi-variant rollout of v2.1 and v2.1-q8 variants for a high-traffic customer, automated rollback logic failed to revert a subset of canaries. Approximately 12% of requests during the incident were routed to incompatible variants, causing increased latency, a measurable regression in output quality for a downstream evaluation suite, and degraded throughput for affected customers. This ticket contains the post-incident analysis, timeline, and concrete action items (runbook, tests, controller fixes, and observability additions).
impact_summary: Duration ~42 minutes (partial recovery at 2025-02-18T15:12Z, full stabilization at 2025-02-18T15:58Z). ~12% of traffic to the rollout was misrouted resulting in 3x error-rate spike for the affected route and ~25% token-cost increase due to retries. Two paying customers reported elevated latency; one filed a support ticket tied to generation regressions.
timeline: 2025-02-18T14:30Z - Rollout started: v2.1 and v2.1-q8 canary slices (5% traffic)
2025-02-18T14:44Z - First latency alerts on route /generate (p95 spiking from 420ms to 1.8s)
2025-02-18T14:50Z - Canary health check failures observed: model internal consistency checks returned mismatch for KV cache schema
2025-02-18T14:55Z - Automated rollback triggered by policy, but controller reported partial failures (some canaries rolled back, others remained pinned)
2025-02-18T15:12Z - Manual intervention: ops ran emergency abort and corrected version pinning for two canary pools
2025-02-18T15:30Z - A/B routing audit found race condition between rollout controller and autoscaler when reclaiming capacity
2025-02-18T15:58Z - All pools stabilized and traffic routing normalized, incident declared resolved
root_cause: A race condition in the rollout controller combined with an invariant-check gap in canary configuration validation. When the autoscaler reclaimed a node that hosted a partially-initialized v2.1-q8 variant, the controller's rollback path attempted an in-place revert while the node was transitioning, leaving a small set of requests routed to a misinitialized model variant. The rollback logic assumed idempotent state transitions and did not validate final routing state before confirming success.
resolution_summary: Manual correction of version pins for affected pools and an emergency abort of the rollout completed recovery. Engineers removed the misinitialized nodes from the router pool, forced reinitialization with the correct KV cache schema, and revalidated the canary health checks. Follow-up: implement atomic rollback acknowledgements and pre-rollback validation checks.
decision_log: Short-term: Add a safety check in the rollout controller to verify that nodes are fully initialized (KV schema sanity) before considering rollback complete
Short-term: Enable 'strict-route-confirm' flag for high-traffic tenants as a temporary mitigation
Medium-term: Design an idempotent two-phase rollback protocol with explicit commit/abort phases
Long-term: Add canary isolation mode to prevent autoscaler reclaim from racing with rollout operations

tests_and_checks: Add CI job that spins up a small cluster and runs rollback+autoscaler stress for 30 minutes
Add e2e smoke test that asserts no requests are served by nodes in 'initializing' state
Add nightly regression eval that runs prompt set used by customer impacted to detect quality regressions early

open_questions: Should we default to 'strict-route-confirm' for dedicated customers?
What SLA/contract language should trigger immediate manual rollback vs auto-rollback?
Is there a way to make KV cache schema negotiation backwards compatible to avoid similar issues?
notes: Ops observed that the controller logs lacked correlation IDs for per-node rollback confirmation — adding these will help future postmortems
This incident affected both hosted and dedicated tenants; consider tenant-scope rollout isolation as a hardening step
Recommend adding a 'canary non-overlap' guard to prevent concurrent rollouts touching the same hash ring slots
